lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.27 - A Listen. Then act it out.

details: Listen develops listening comprehension through a story that recycles target language. Then act it out practises speaking skills.
Look for careful listening, comprehension of the story  and repetition of the story with fluent speaking and correct pronunciation.
“Let’s visit our friends today. I’d like to go to Amy’s house. Will you come too?”

Heads Up (Reading): 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and help Ss to understand the text by asking questions, practicing skimming (reading for gist), scanning (reading for specific information) and detail (reading for comprehension). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down (Listen and Follow): 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together (Video, then act it out): 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.28 - B. Look and circle

details: Look and circle allows students to recognise key vocabulary by linking it to single-word options for them to circle. The activity reinforces meaning as students look at the pictures and choose the correct answer.
Look for students reading possible answers and checking each picture carefully and circling correct answers.
“Tina’s so cute! I can’t believe we saw her learn a new activity while we were there!”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

Homework Check:

Project Gallery:

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.81 - A Read and number

details: Read and number develops reading and comprehension through ordering a story, reinforcing comprehension and reading fluency and pronunciation with accurate word stress.
Look for correct and logical story order, clear pronunciation, accurate word and phrase stress, confident reading.
“Let’s go to Elsa’s house next!”

Reward moment

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.28 - C Make your own story

details: Make your own story develops confidence with writing skills by asking students to select words to complete  a short story. It supports sentence building and meaningful language use.
Look for comprehension, confidence in making word choices and in acting out their stories.
“I loved meeting Elsa’s sister. But I really want to see Tina again. Shall we go back and see what she’s doing now?”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.28 - Tongue Twisters Listen and say

details: Tongue Twisters: Listen and say helps students practice pronunciation and repetition of the short e sound  as they listen and repeat the tongue twisters.
Look for careful listening, confident pronunciation and accurate repetition.
“Tina  and Emily can do lots of things! Can you do something tricky? Can you say these tongue twisters with me?”
